key_insight: Large-eddy simulations show that lateral constriction can trigger plunging flows in bedrock channels, with the optimal constriction shifting from about 35% at lower flow to about 50% at higher flow.
engineering_relevance: These results help improve bedrock incision and landscape-evolution models by capturing nonuniform, high-shear, and intermittent flow dynamics rather than assuming steady flow.
method: Eddy-resolving large-eddy simulations (LES) of laboratory-scale bedrock-channel flows
Parametric testing of channel constriction under lower- and higher-discharge conditions
Analysis of velocity inversion, shear stress, velocity variance, and plunging intermittency
evidence_signal: The simulations identified constriction-dependent velocity inversions and showed that higher discharge increases shear stress, velocity variance, and pulsing near the plunge point.
watch_item: Results come from laboratory-scale LES, so direct transfer to field-scale rivers will require careful calibration and validation.
paper_title: Large Eddy Simulation of Plunging Flows in Laboratory-Scale Bedrock Rivers
